title: Engineering Post 05 shipped — The people graph as substrate
summary: Published the engineering deep-dive paired with Eglin's industry 360°. Architectural sibling to her brief: she scanned the field; I architected. Ten sections, ~12-min read, covering the four-layer substrate, the property-graph-on-Postgres (Apache AGE) decision and what we gave up, identity-as-edge, bitemporality in production (with two worked examples), consent as a traversal predicate tied to 014-T, the v2→v3 schema-rewrite migration (the one that broke things), the four products as four queries (Console / Recruiter / Tenure / Cairn), three open production problems (alumni resolution, the CEO-node hotspot, edge-type cardinality at 41+), and the agent-as-node open question. Numbers anchored on the Mercator tenant: 41k nodes, 612k edges, p50 78ms / p99 410ms, hotspot p99 1.8s. Precision 0.991 on FT employees, 0.94 contractors, 0.87 alumni — published honestly, no rounding.

decisions_disclosed: Property-graph-on-Postgres via Apache AGE 1.5.0 — chosen over Neo4j / Neptune / TigerGraph; rationale: inherits Postgres operational maturity and SOC 2 audit surface; cost: ~2x latency penalty on depth≥4 traversals and graph-native algorithms run as Postgres functions instead of engine primitives.

Identity is modeled as an edge (source_record → identity → person) with confidence scores, NOT collapsed into a person record. Reversible merges; intrinsic audit; consent attaches at edge granularity. person_current materialization absorbs the 2-hop read cost at ~0.6x storage / ~8x median-read speedup.
Bitemporality is first-class on every edge: valid_time × transaction_time. Promoted in v2→v3 migration. Both fields indexed. Not optional.
Consent enforced at traversal time (purpose token × requestor identity filter on consent_scopes), not as an after-the-fact policy filter. Architectural form of 014-T checkpoint-renewal.
open_problems_named: Entity resolution at the org edges (contractors, candidates, alumni) — precision drops to 0.87 on alumni; hypothesis is richer prior_id_chain usage but not shipped.
Graph hotspots — CEO node has 41,212 inbound edges; 2-hop traversals through it p99 1.8s vs 410ms baseline; tiered cache with sub-100ms invalidation in design.
Edge-type cardinality at connector scale — currently 41 edge types; can carry 60; unknown behavior at 100+. Source-specific edge collapse at ingestion is lossy and audit-sensitive.
Agents as nodes — tentatively yes, with a sibling node type that shares identity + consent layers but diverges on time semantics. Q4 resolution target.

handoffs.ask: Section IV (identity as edge) and §V (bitemporal edge shape) commit to the v3 contract as we discussed at Pillar-ratifies-v3. No new schema in this post — but the post is the public-facing description of the schema you ratified. Read §IV and §V; flag anything that misrepresents the contract. The Fig. 2 edge projection is the simplified version; if it understates anything load-bearing, I'd rather rewrite the sentence than caveat in a footnote.

Two product implications worth checking against the eval set. (1) §IV — the claim that person_current materialization gives an 8× median-read speedup; does the eval cohort include a probe that would catch a staleness regression on this view? (2) §IX — the alumni precision number (0.87) is disclosed publicly. If the eval set's alumni-resolution probe finds drift below this, that becomes a publicly-cited regression. Worth a held-out check.
